reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry, albuterol 4 puffs via spacer. Three acceptable, repeatable efforts. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.61. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 64% of predicted. No significant bronchodilator response. Flow-volume loop with expiratory scooping, inspiratory limb normal.
reports.conclusion: Moderate airflow obstruction, consistent with COPD.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back for COPD f/u and spirometry. Winter's been ok. Job sites slow in January so he's less winded than in summer. Albuterol a couple times a month. No sputum color change, no fevers.

Vitals per flowsheet. Lungs with reduced air entry bilaterally, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

Spirometry today: post-BD FEV1/FVC 0.61, FEV1 64% predicted. Moderate obstruction, confirms the COPD label he came with.

Plan:
- Stay on tiotropium daily, albuterol prn. He's comfortable and not interested in adding a second inhaler.
- PCV20 given today.
- Shared decision visit for lung cancer screening: eligible at 51 with 35 pack-years and still smoking. Went over false positives, radiation, the chance of more scans. He wants it. LDCT ordered.
- Still smoking about a pack a day. Asked again about help quitting; he says maybe in the spring.

RTC 3 months for BP.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast, 1.25 mm reconstructions. CTDIvol within screening protocol limits.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation or pleural effusion. Heart normal in size, no pericardial effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: Lung screening CT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Keith, the screening CT of your lungs showed no nodules or spots. That's the best category. The plan is to repeat it every year while you qualify, so next one is due around February 2026. Still happy to help with quitting whenever you're ready.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Early slot before work. BP f/u. Taking amlodipine every day, no swelling, no headaches. Breathing the same as winter, back on a crew full time.

BP at goal on the flowsheet. Heart RRR. Lungs diminished, clear. No pedal edema.

A/P
HTN controlled on amlodipine 5, no change.
COPD stable on tiotropium.
Tobacco: still smoking. Brief counseling, declines meds. 
Shingrix #1 today, explained he may feel lousy for a day. #2 in 2 to 6 months.
F/u in about 2 months then annual in the fall.

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he's in his truck after work, verbal consent for video visit, location in MA confirmed.

Heat makes the breathing harder on roofs but no worse than other summers. Using albuterol maybe twice a week right now, usually midafternoon. No fever, no change in phlegm. Taking amlodipine. No home BP cuff.

No exam beyond appearance: talking comfortably, no audible wheeze, not using accessory muscles.

A/P: COPD at his baseline, HTN on amlodipine without issues. Refills sent for all 3. Annual visit in October with labs, 2nd Shingrix and flu then. Reminded him the lung CT is yearly.

documents.title: Annual visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Keith, you're due for your yearly physical and fall shots. We have Friday 10/24 at 8:00 open. Want it?

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 52 now. Feels fine. Breathing at his usual, summer was the worst of it and it's eased with cooler weather. Albuterol a few times a month. Denies chest pain, ankle swelling or coughing blood; weight steady.

Meds: tiotropium daily, albuterol prn, amlodipine 5. Takes them.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: still framing and roofing. Still about a pack a day. Alcohol occasional.

Exam: NAD. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No thyromegaly or adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs with diminished breath sounds both sides, no wheezes, no crackles. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without lesions of concern. Extremities without edema, good pulses.

PHQ-9: 2.

Assessment and plan
- COPD, moderate on spirometry, stable on tiotropium. Continue.
- HTN controlled on amlodipine 5.
- Tobacco use: 35+ pack-years. Again discussed quitting, offered patch or varenicline; he says not this year. Lung screening CT due again in February, he knows.
- Prevention: flu, updated COVID and Shingrix #2 today (series complete). FIT kit given. BMP, CBC, lipids drawn.
- Return in 6 months, sooner if his breathing changes or he gets a chest cold that doesn't clear.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Keith, everything from Friday is normal: kidney function, salts, blood counts and cholesterol. Nothing to change. Send the FIT back when you can.

documents.body: FIT negative, patient notified by portal. Recall set for 1 year.
